reason: Safe and sensible. Marisol asked to go back to 40 miles and start speedwork. The draft says "not yet" straight away and explains why: going from 12 to 40 is a 28-mile step. Next week adds up to about 23 easy miles, with the long run at 7. That's a reasonable step back up from a 12-mile recovery week for someone who has been running about 41 miles a week. Speed is held back until her legs have had one more easy week, so she isn't rushed back. There's no pain or illness to work around. The plan keeps her usual rest days (Mon and Fri) and puts the long run on Sunday. Each day can be run as written, with a distance, an effort cue and a sensible easy pace (9:50–10:20/mi against a 3:45 goal). The draft also answers the 10K part of her question with a clear way to bring structure back in. I took one point off for details the card doesn't support: Thanksgiving, the five-week timeline and the heart rate cap of 140. The draft may have invented these.
